questions.question: What is the kernel of a linear map $A:V\to W$?
options: The set of vectors $v\in V$ such that $Av=0$.
The set of all vectors in $W$ not reached by $A$.
The set of all outputs of $A$.
The set of scalars used by $V$.

questions.question: For a linear map $A\colon V\to W$, in which space does its kernel lie?
options: Outside both the domain and codomain.
In the domain of the map.

questions.question: What is the dimension of the kernel of a linear map called?
What kind of subset is the kernel of a linear map?
options: A subspace of the codomain only.

questions.question: What does $\ker A=\{0\}$ tell us about a linear map?
options: Every vector is sent to zero.
The only vector sent to zero is the zero vector.
The codomain of the map contains only the zero vector.

questions.question: For $A(x,y)=(x,0)$, which vectors are in $\ker A$?
What is the kernel of the identity map $I(v)=v$?
For $A:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R$ given by $A(x,y)=x+y$, which vector lies in $\ker A$?
For the zero map $Z(v)=0$, what is $\ker Z$?
For a linear map $A\colon V\to W$ with $V$ finite-dimensional, what does $\dim(\ker A)+\dim(\operatorname{im}A)$ equal?
Why is the kernel useful for studying injectivity?
options: The kernel is always empty for injective maps.
A map is injective exactly when its kernel is the whole domain.
A linear map is injective exactly when its kernel is $\{0\}$.
Injectivity ignores what happens to zero.

questions.question: Why must the zero vector always belong to the kernel of a linear map?
options: The zero vector is always outside the domain.
Every vector space has no zero vector.
Only the zero map has zero in its kernel.

questions.question: What is the difference between kernel and range?
options: The kernel and range are always the same set.
The kernel is a scalar and the range is a vector.
The kernel is about inputs sent to zero, while the range is about outputs reached.
The kernel is a subset of the codomain, while the range is a subset of the domain.

questions.question: For $A(x,y,z)=(x,z)$, which condition describes $\ker A$?
What is the kernel of an injective linear map?
If $\ker A=\operatorname{span}((1,1))$, which vector is killed by $A$?
If $\dim(\ker A)=2$, how many independent directions does $A$ send to $\boldsymbol0$?
Can the kernel be empty?
options: Yes, if the codomain is larger than the domain.
Yes, if the map is injective.
No, it contains at least the zero vector for a linear map.
No, because it always equals the whole domain.

questions.question: For $A(x,y,z)=x-y$, what is one parametrisation of $\ker A$?
If $A:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R^2$ has $\ker A=\{(0,0)\}$, which statement follows?
options: The kernel is the whole domain.
